succession_policy.tip_seasoned: Field corn is a single full-season crop, not a succession crop. You sow once after the last spring frost and grow the whole block to a dry-down harvest in fall, so there is no staggered replanting. Give it the longest run of frost-free weather you have, since a late sowing may not reach hard dent before frost.
succession_policy.tip_beginner: You plant field corn once and grow it the whole season, so there is no need to replant every couple of weeks. Sow after the last frost and give it plenty of time, because it needs a long, warm season to dry down before fall.

verification_status.verification_log: field_corn_gs_arc 2026-07-15 (first dry-corn of the corn family; clones the certified sweet-corn warm_season_grass section-E shell and re-points it to a single full-season DENT crop grown to a dry-down grain harvest). ARCHETYPE warm_season_grass, frost_anchored, direct-sown block-planted. HARVEST: dry ear at hard dent / black layer (husks brown+papery, kernels hard+dented ~30-35% moisture, cured to 13-15% for storage) -- a 9-stage from-sow ladder germination->seedling->vegetative->tasseling->silking->kernel_fill->dry_down->harvest->cure_thresh; harvest_window_days OMITTED (one-shot dry harvest); succession_policy suitable:false (single full-season crop, dry-bean pattern); harvest_urgency low. VARIETIES: legacy shape only (no maturity_class -> NOT in variety_detail_gate scope); open-pollinated dents John Haulk + Cocke's Prolific (clemson_hgic) + a modern grain hybrid by relative maturity (umn_ext); Reid's Yellow Dent / Bloody Butcher named in prose only. PROVISIONAL: crop-level days_to_maturity [95,120] mid 110 is a SYNTHESIS (Trevor ratifies at promote) from convergent extension figures -- Clemson HGIC 'from 90 to 120 days after planting for most varieties', Bloody Butcher 105-110d, and grain-hybrid relative-maturity ranges; no single T1 quotes the exact band. REGIONS: 12 T1-anchored single-crop calendars, Option C (all plantable): humid regions (fl_peninsula, se_gulf, hawaii_tropical, rgv, pnw) carry a field-drying advisory (harvest at hard dent, finish indoors); short-season northern + desert cells carry an honest marginal/early-only advisory; deserts keep the corn heat_pause; rgv frost-free off-season = season_over; harvest shifted later than sweet corn for the longer grain maturity. CROSS-POLLINATION honesty: dent pollen crosses sweet corn to starchy + kills popcorn pop -> isolate ~300 ft or stagger tasseling ~2 weeks (distance harmonized to the family-protective 300 ft the popcorn sources iastate_ext + umn_ext state; ncsu_ext backs the mechanism + stagger). source_set all T1 (clemson_hgic + the sweet-corn corn source set), 0 non-T1, 0 uncatalogued. See docs/reviews/notes/2026-07-15/corn_field_sourcing.md.

field_additions.note: field-corn (dent) timing spine: propagule=seed, dtm_anchor=from_sow, direct-sown block-planted grass; 9-stage germination->dry_down->harvest->cure_thresh dry-down ladder to DTM [95,120] (mid 110); harvest_window_days OMITTED (one-shot dry harvest); thin_to [8,12], sow_depth [1,2].
planting_layout 'block' + pollination_block_min_rows 4 carried from the sweet-corn warm_season_grass pattern (wind pollination -> plant a block of >=4 short rows).

open_findings.summary: [CORRECTED same day, 2026-08-10: this finding first called the DTM MODELED; that mischaracterized the crop's own records.] The 110 to 120 day dry-down figure in se_gulf harvest prose is a narrowing WITHIN the cert-ratified days_to_maturity [95,120], which the crop's verification_log records as a SYNTHESIS Trevor ratified at certification from convergent extension figures, first among them Clemson HGIC "from 90 to 120 days after planting for most varieties". That document (hgic.clemson.edu/homegrown-grits/, home-garden register, dent corn) was re-found and READ 2026-08-10: it publishes the 90-120 band, the husk cue and the drying guidance, and now anchors both harvest arms for the claims it publishes; the exact 110-120 sentence rests on the ratified synthesis. uga_b577 removed from the harvest arms and retained on the sow arms. DO NOT repoint these arms at B577's Corn row: it reads 80-100 days (home-garden sweet corn) and CONTRADICTS this crop's band. MU IPM's relative-maturity 98-120 read and not cited (an RM rating is not a calendar DTM).
open_findings.basis: PLA-156 dispositions; the modeled call was held by the claude.ai lane, verified here, and corrected. Cert record: field-corn.verification_status.verification_log, PROVISIONAL band synthesis.

direct_sow.label: primary
direct_sow.synthesis_note_seasoned: Field corn for Northern Tier (Cold Zones): direct-sow once into warm soil (at least 60°F) after the last spring frost (frost-free regions anchor to the regional planting calendar), a single full-season block grown to a dry-down grain harvest. No succession: field corn is sown once and dried down in place.

harvest_start.label: primary
harvest_start.synthesis_note_seasoned: The block reaches its dry-down grain harvest about 110 to 120 days after sowing, when the husks are brown and papery and the kernels are hard and dented.

harvest_end.label: primary
harvest_end.synthesis_note_seasoned: Harvest ends when the dried ears are all in. Sound ears can field-dry on the stalk in good weather; in humid weather they are pulled at hard dent and finished drying under cover.

Corn sources retained.

3.zone_notes: Short season: a full-season dent barely finishes here. Choose the earliest grain variety you can find, sow as soon as the soil warms, and expect to pick at hard dent and finish drying indoors, since the crop may not fully dry on the stalk before frost.

northern_tier.region_notes_seasoned: Field corn is a warm-season crop here, sown once the soil reaches 60°F, roughly two weeks after the last spring frost. Season length is the binding constraint for a 95-to-120-day dent: favor early grain varieties, sow at the first warm soil, and in the shortest zones pick at hard dent and cure under cover, since the crop may not fully field-dry before frost.
northern_tier.region_notes_beginner: In cold-winter regions, sow field corn only after the last frost, once the soil has warmed to at least 60°F, usually a couple of weeks past your frost date. Summers are short, so choose the earliest grain varieties and sow promptly; in the coldest zones the crop may need to finish drying indoors after a fall frost.

8.zone_notes: Humid region: corn dries down slowly here and ears can mold in the field. Harvest at hard dent when the kernels are firm, then pull back the husks and finish drying the ears indoors with good airflow before shelling.

se_gulf.region_notes_seasoned: The humid Southeast grows field corn as a spring-sown crop that dries down in the heat of summer. The load-bearing risk is a wet, humid finish that molds ripening ears, so harvest at hard dent and cure the ears under cover with airflow rather than leaving them to field-dry.
se_gulf.region_notes_beginner: In the Southeast and Gulf, sow field corn in spring after the last frost and grow it to a summer dry-down. Summers are hot and humid, so the ears may finish drying poorly on the stalk; pick them at hard dent and dry them indoors.

ca_interior.region_notes_beginner: In California's hot interior valleys, sow field corn from late spring and grow it to a fall dry-down. The long, dry season suits a full-season dent, and the dry autumn air finishes the grain well on the stalk.

9.zone_notes: Marginal, early-only: sow at the first warm soil so the crop dries down before the summer heat shuts down pollination. Use the fastest early grain variety, since a full-season dent runs short of time here.

heat_pause.basis_seasoned: Deep summer in the low desert runs far too hot for corn to pollinate: sustained highs well over 95°F kill pollen and desiccate the silks, so no reliable ears set from a midsummer planting. The crop is grown in the cooler months instead.
