succession_policy.tip_seasoned: Popcorn is a single full-season crop, not a succession crop. You sow once after the last spring frost and grow the whole block to a dry-down harvest in fall, so there is no staggered replanting. Give it the longest run of frost-free weather you have, since a late sowing may not dry down before frost.
succession_policy.tip_beginner: You plant popcorn once and grow it the whole season, so there is no need to replant every couple of weeks. Sow after the last frost and give it plenty of time, because it needs a long, warm season to dry down before fall.

verification_status.verification_log: popcorn_gs_arc 2026-07-15 (second dry-corn of the corn family; clones the certified sweet-corn warm_season_grass section-E shell and re-points it to a single full-season POPCORN crop grown to a dry-down and cured to popping moisture). ARCHETYPE warm_season_grass, frost_anchored, direct-sown block-planted. HARVEST: dry ear at hard-dry / physiological maturity (husks brown+papery, kernels hard+glassy), then cured to the popping window ~13-14% moisture with a test-pop check -- a 9-stage from-sow ladder germination->seedling->vegetative->tasseling->silking->kernel_fill->dry_down->harvest->cure_thresh; harvest_window_days OMITTED (one-shot dry harvest); succession_policy suitable:false (single full-season crop, dry-bean pattern); harvest_urgency low. VARIETIES: legacy shape only (no maturity_class -> NOT in variety_detail_gate scope); Iowa State home-garden variety table rows Tom Thumb 85d, Robust R128YH 103d, Gourmet Mushroom 103d, Strawberry De-Lite 98d (iastate_ext); Japanese Hulless + Dakota Black named in prose only (seed-trade, no T1 DTM). PROVISIONAL: crop-level days_to_maturity [90,110] mid 100 is a SYNTHESIS (Trevor ratifies at promote) from convergent extension figures -- Iowa State variety table 85-112d, UMN 'most varieties require 90 to 120 days'; no single T1 quotes the exact band. REGIONS: 12 T1-anchored single-crop calendars, Option C (all plantable): humid regions (fl_peninsula, se_gulf, hawaii_tropical, rgv, pnw) carry a field-drying advisory (harvest at hard-dry, finish indoors); short-season northern + desert cells carry an honest marginal/early-only advisory (early dwarf like Tom Thumb helps); deserts keep the corn heat_pause; rgv frost-free off-season = season_over. CROSS-POLLINATION honesty (the sharpest isolation case): popcorn is the VICTIM -- ANY foreign pollen, sweet OR dent, crossing onto the ear keeps it from popping -> isolate at least 300 ft or stagger tasseling ~2 weeks (300 ft cited to the iastate_ext + umn_ext popcorn pages, both verbatim; ~2-week/14-day tassel-stagger lever from the iastate_ext sweet-corn home-garden guide). POPPING MOISTURE: cure to ~13-14%, over-dry will not pop (iastate_ext, umn_ext). source_set all T1 (iastate_ext + umn_ext + the sweet-corn corn source set), 0 non-T1, 0 uncatalogued. See docs/reviews/notes/2026-07-15/corn_popcorn_sourcing.md.

direct_sow.synthesis_note_seasoned: Popcorn for Northern Tier (Cold Zones): direct-sow once into warm soil (at least 60°F) after the last spring frost (frost-free regions anchor to the regional planting calendar), a single full-season block grown to a dry-down harvest and then cured to popping moisture. No succession: popcorn is sown once and dried down in place.

harvest_start.label: primary
harvest_start.synthesis_note_seasoned: The block reaches its dry-down harvest about 100 to 110 days after sowing, when the husks are brown and papery and the kernels are hard and glossy; the crop is then cured to the popping window (about 13 to 14 percent moisture).

harvest_end.label: primary
harvest_end.synthesis_note_seasoned: Harvest ends when the dried ears are all in. Sound ears can field-dry on the stalk in good weather; in humid weather they are picked at hard-dry and finished drying under cover.

3.zone_notes: Short season: popcorn barely finishes here. Choose the earliest variety you can find (an early dwarf like Tom Thumb), sow as soon as the soil warms, and expect to pick at hard-dry and finish drying indoors, since the crop may not fully dry on the stalk before frost.

northern_tier.region_notes_seasoned: Popcorn is a warm-season crop here, sown once the soil reaches 60°F, roughly two weeks after the last spring frost. Season length is the binding constraint for a 90-to-110-day crop: favor early varieties like Tom Thumb, sow at the first warm soil, and in the shortest zones pick at hard-dry and cure under cover, since the crop may not fully field-dry before frost.
northern_tier.region_notes_beginner: In cold-winter regions, sow popcorn only after the last frost, once the soil has warmed to at least 60°F, usually a couple of weeks past your frost date. Summers are short, so choose an early variety and sow promptly; in the coldest zones the ears may need to finish drying indoors after a fall frost.

se_gulf.region_notes_seasoned: The humid Southeast grows popcorn as a spring-sown crop that dries down in the heat of summer. The load-bearing risk is a wet, humid finish that molds ripening ears, so harvest at hard-dry and cure the ears under cover with airflow rather than leaving them to field-dry.
se_gulf.region_notes_beginner: In the Southeast and Gulf, sow popcorn in spring after the last frost and grow it to a summer dry-down. Summers are hot and humid, so the ears may finish drying poorly on the stalk; pick them at hard-dry and finish drying them indoors.

ca_interior.region_notes_beginner: In California's hot interior valleys, sow popcorn from late spring and grow it to a fall dry-down. The long, dry season suits a full-season crop, and the dry autumn air finishes the kernels well on the stalk.

9.zone_notes: Marginal, early-only: sow at the first warm soil so the crop dries down before the summer heat shuts down pollination. Use a fast early variety, since a full-season popcorn runs short of time here.

heat_pause.basis_seasoned: Deep summer in the low desert runs far too hot for corn to pollinate: sustained highs well over 95°F kill pollen and desiccate the silks, so no reliable ears set from a midsummer planting. The crop is grown in the cooler months instead.

ca_desert.region_notes_beginner: In the low-desert of California, grow popcorn as an early-spring crop that finishes before the lethal summer heat. Only the faster early varieties fit the short cool window, so sow at the first warm soil in February.
